questions.question: The decontamination corridor is located in the:
questions.rationale: Decon happens in the warm (contamination reduction) zone.

questions.question: The treatment area should be:
options: B. Inside the hot zone for speed
D. In the cold zone, upwind, next to the loading zone
questions.rationale: Safety plus flow: cold zone, upwind, adjacent to the loading zone.

questions.question: Which part of the treatment area should be closest to the ambulance loading exit?
Ambulances should move through the scene:
options: B. On a one-way loop: staging → loading zone → hospital
C. By reversing into the treatment area
D. Only after all patients are treated
questions.rationale: One-way vehicle flow keeps the scene moving and safe.

questions.question: A suspected pipe bomb is found near the treatment area. The minimum mandatory evacuation distance is approximately:
questions.rationale: ≈70 ft mandatory; ≈1,200 ft preferred outdoor evacuation per stand-off charts — move the treatment area.

questions.question: The helicopter landing zone should be placed:
options: B. In the cold zone away from the treatment area
C. On the access road used by ambulances
D. Next to the red treatment area
questions.rationale: Rotor wash throws debris; the LZ also shouldn't block ground flow.

questions.question: Which statement about zones is TRUE?
options: A. Zones can move as wind, threat, or structure changes
B. The cold zone has no hazards ever
D. Zones are fixed once set
questions.rationale: Re-evaluate zones continuously, especially wind in chemical incidents.

questions.question: Staging during a suspected terrorist bombing should be:
options: B. Next to the blast site
C. At the most obvious nearby parking lot
D. Out of sight, in a location checked for secondary devices
questions.rationale: Secondary devices may target predictable responder gathering points.
